### P0 · Progression & pacing

> “You can also adjust the upgrade prices and income rates to make sure progression feels rewarding without becoming too easy or too slow.”  
> — [GuideRealm – How To Make An ENTIRE Roblox Game With AI - Full Guide @ 7:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ltbZzXRrDF8&t=452s) · YouTube

> “of the challenge and at the end I'll give my thoughts on the engine and I'll explain whether or not I think you should learn it depending on your skill level and goals and if you already know that you”  
> — [BinzuDev – How I Learned To Make Roblox Games in a Week @ 0:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vUN2cJD4mUk&t=30s) · YouTube

> “Make a starter pack that helps with progression. Add some limited-time items.”  
> — [janisjanis01 – How I Made a Viral Roblox Game @ 3:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fjlOaEALWmg&t=182s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Model cost and reward curves in a spreadsheet first; target a predictable time-to-next-upgrade at each stage.
1. Show the next unlock and progress toward it permanently on the HUD.
1. Re-tune curves from analytics (progression/economy events), not intuition.

**APIs / tools:** `AnalyticsService:LogEconomyEvent`, `AnalyticsService custom events for level-ups`

**Measure:** Median time to each milestone; Drop-off by level; Sink/source ratio of soft currency

**Pitfalls:** Exponential costs with linear rewards (a hidden wall); No visible next goal

### P1 · Action -> reward -> upgrade cycle

> “If you're making a simulator, make sure the gameplay loop works. Or even for a horror game, just start small and then expand.”  
> — [DitchyDevelopments – How To Make Your First Roblox Game in 2026 (With AI) @ 2:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v8vby3iOOX4&t=136s) · YouTube

> “And you need to be original. You need to make an original gameplay loop, something to stand out.”  
> — [Laugh – I Accidentally Made a Viral Roblox Game @ 9:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WFyrlstSDe4&t=591s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Write the loop as a single sentence (verb -> reward -> spend -> stronger verb) and make every system feed it.
1. Keep the minute-to-minute action responsive on its own; the reward/upgrade layer amplifies a fun verb, it cannot replace one.
1. Make one full loop completable within the first minute, then lengthen loops gradually.

**APIs / tools:** `DataStoreService (UpdateAsync) for currency/upgrade persistence`, `RemoteEvents with server-side validation`

**Measure:** Loops completed per session; Average session length; D1 retention

**Pitfalls:** Rewards that do not change how the next loop plays; Trusting client-reported rewards (exploitable)

### P1 · Concept & hook

> “And you need to be original. You need to make an original gameplay loop, something to stand out.”  
> — [Laugh – I Accidentally Made a Viral Roblox Game @ 9:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WFyrlstSDe4&t=591s) · YouTube

> “so earlier I did say that I wouldn't try to make the game idea I had”  
> — [BinzuDev – How I Learned To Make Roblox Games in a Week @ 16:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vUN2cJD4mUk&t=1013s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Validate the hook before building systems: can the idea be understood from the icon and title in 2 seconds?
1. Study the top games in the genre; ship the genre's expected loop, then differentiate on one axis.

**Measure:** Thumbnail click-through rate; First-play bounce rate

**Pitfalls:** Novelty with no repeatable loop; Copying a trend after it has peaked

### P1 · Scarcity & FOMO

> “Make a starter pack that helps with progression. Add some limited-time items.”  
> — [janisjanis01 – How I Made a Viral Roblox Game @ 3:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fjlOaEALWmg&t=182s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

### P1 · Daily rewards & streaks

> “All right? You want to have a strong curiosity hook, strong reason to come back tomorrow.”  
> — [Tizzy RBLX – My Roblox Game Makes $119,300/mo (38K CCU, here's how) @ 16:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LZOohZHsJus&t=965s) · YouTube

> “Day one retention is how many people play the game and then come back the next day.”  
> — [Laugh – I Accidentally Made a Viral Roblox Game @ 7:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WFyrlstSDe4&t=438s) · YouTube

**Numbers cited:** `Day one retention is how`

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Track lastClaimDay and streak server-side in UTC days (os.time() // 86400); never trust client time.
1. Escalate rewards across a 7-day cycle with a highlight on day 7; show tomorrow's reward to create intent.
1. Use a forgiving streak (grace day or partial reset) so one missed day does not erase the habit.

**APIs / tools:** `DataStoreService:UpdateAsync (atomic claim)`, `ExperienceNotificationService:PromptOptIn for 'reward ready' reminders`

**Measure:** D1 / D7 retention; Daily claim rate; Streak length distribution

**Pitfalls:** Double claims from a race between servers (use UpdateAsync); Rewards so large they distort the economy

**Measure:** Misclick / back-out rate on menus; Purchase prompt reach

**Pitfalls:** Pixel-sized UI that breaks on mobile; Shop buttons covering the play area

### P1 · Onboarding funnel measurement & experiments

> “Uh, and I'm just going to walk you through step by step everything you need to know, and by the end of the game or end of the video, you'll have made the game that I just showed you at”

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Instrument every onboarding step with LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent (ordered, one-time per player).
1. Use LogFunnelStepEvent for recurring funnels (shop flow, quest chains) and Journeys for branching paths.
1. Fix the largest drop-off first, then A/B test the fix with Experiments, broken down by player segment (new vs returning, U18 vs 18+).

**APIs / tools:** `AnalyticsService:LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent`, `AnalyticsService:LogFunnelStepEvent`, `Analytics > Journeys`, `Experiments (segmentation & targeting)`

**Measure:** Step-to-step conversion; Overall onboarding completion

**Pitfalls:** Too many steps to read the funnel; Logging steps from the client

### P1 · Friction & cognitive load

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Introduce one concept at a time and confirm understanding through action.

**Measure:** Funnel drop-off per step

**Pitfalls:** Multiple currencies explained at once; Popups stacking on join

### P1 · Mobile & cross-platform input

### P1 · First session & first impression

> “So, I will explain this in the easiest way possible because this may be a little complex for you, especially if it's your first time.”  
> — [MikoLikesHat – How to ACTUALLY LEARN to Script in Roblox Studio (5 Steps to learn) @ 3:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GE6Z1n57yDU&t=186s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Spawn new players directly into the core action; defer menus, lore and settings.
1. Script the first 60 seconds: first action, first reward, first upgrade.
1. Detect first-time players server-side and give them the guided path; skip it for returners.

**APIs / tools:** `AnalyticsService:LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent`, `DataStoreService (hasCompletedTutorial flag)`

**Measure:** Onboarding funnel step completion; First-play bounce rate; D1 retention

**Pitfalls:** Loading screens and text walls before play; Same tutorial for returning players

> “[clears throat] Build the item, place it into your tycoon, give it a name, create a button, give the button heroid, add a price, add what you need to buy first before the button appears, link it to your item,”  
> — [Duckable – How FAST Can I Make a Roblox Game? @ 8:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dp7vw20e-fA&t=537s) · YouTube

> “Make a starter pack that helps with progression. Add some limited-time items.”

> “Nine times out of 10, you want to anchor all of your builds or you're going to be in for a lagging nightmare the bigger your map gets.”  
> — [RoBuilder – ABSOLUTE Beginner Basics.. Roblox Studio For Noobs 2025 @ 6:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-5OOovmkJss&t=383s) · YouTube

**Numbers cited:** `mine to be 20 Robux . Really cheap`

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Build a price ladder: a low-friction starter offer, core items, and premium bundles that anchor value.
1. Use Price Optimization and Regional Pricing instead of guessing; re-test after major updates.
1. Read prices with GetProductInfo on the client so price-optimisation tests show each player their price.
1. Sell the first purchase cheaply (tens of Robux); many small payers beat one big spender for retention and discovery.

**APIs / tools:** `Price Optimization (Creator Hub)`, `Regional pricing`, `MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo`

**Measure:** Conversion by price point; Revenue per DAU

**Pitfalls:** Only high price points (no first purchase); Constant discounts training players to wait

### P1 · Paid random items (eggs, crates)

> “So, right now, the eggs don't work right. And I think what I need to do is tell the client to throw the eggs instead of the server. In non stupid nerd words, we need to give the player's device control over the eggs so …”  
> — [Duckable – Can I Make a VIRAL TYCOON in 24 HOURS? @ 10:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F9sfnpkzcPw&t=608s) · YouTube

> “We are perfectly engineering this to make sure there is no way to somehow pay Robux and buy these loot boxes.”  
> — [Laugh – I Accidentally Made a Viral Roblox Game @ 11:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WFyrlstSDe4&t=701s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. If you sell random items, disclose odds before purchase and keep items earnable through play.
1. Check PolicyService for each player and offer a direct-purchase path where paid random items are restricted.

**APIs / tools:** `PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync (ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted)`

**Measure:** Conversion vs refund/complaint signals; Retention of payers

**Pitfalls:** Undisclosed odds (policy violation); Ignoring regional restrictions

### P1 · Developer products (consumables)

> “so if you want both of those things make sure you watch this whole video throughout even if you skip 10 seconds you might miss something important and it won't work you as you might be like this guy yeah”  
> — [Reckless - Roblox – How To MAKE a ROBLOX GAME on MOBILE... @ 1:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KXAYJ5TnKH4&t=78s) · YouTube

**Numbers cited:** `if you skip 10 seconds you might miss`

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Sell consumables (boosts, currency packs, revives) as developer products.
1. Grant inside MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt and return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is saved; dedupe by PurchaseId.
1. Offer products in context (revive on death, boost before a hard section) and allow buying several consumables at once.
1. Order the shop per player with the product intelligence APIs (RankProductsAsync once at join; RecommendTopProductsAsync via task.spawn).
1. Subscribe to the Transaction Refunded webhook and claw back refunded developer-product grants in your own data.

**APIs / tools:** `MarketplaceService:PromptProductPurchase`, `MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt`, `RankProductsAsync / RecommendTopProductsAsync`, `Transaction Refunded webhook`, `AnalyticsService:LogEconomyEvent`

**Measure:** Payer conversion; ARPPU; Repeat purchase rate; Refund rate

**Pitfalls:** Granting before persisting (lost purchases); Non-idempotent receipt handling (double grants); Broken ProcessReceipt blocks sales of Listed products outside the game

### P1 · Ads (rewarded, immersive, sponsored)

> “So instead of just going out and you know putting a YouTube sponsor like before this video for example, they can build something that's interactive in Roblox and that's the new way to make people into kind of lifelong fans.”  
> — [Starter Story – I Spent 24 Hours With Roblox Millionaires @ 4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xgnm6SynH4&t=295s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Treat rewarded ads as opt-in value exchanges placed at natural pauses.
1. Use Ads Manager campaigns to buy acquisition only after onboarding converts well.

**APIs / tools:** `Ads Manager (Creator Hub)`, `Immersive ads`

**Measure:** Cost per acquired player vs their D7 value

**Pitfalls:** Paying to acquire players into a leaky funnel

### P1 · Conversion & revenue KPIs

> “You need to understand marketing, game design, retention, monetization, balancing, psychology, and more. It's not a get-richqu scheme.”  
> — [waveshine – Watch this before making ROBLOX Games @ 1:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xnlaYLnCtFc&t=65s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Log every purchase and currency flow with LogEconomyEvent to see sources, sinks and paths to purchase.
1. Increase conversion by placing offers where players feel the need, not by adding more offers.

**APIs / tools:** `AnalyticsService:LogEconomyEvent`, `Creator Hub Analytics: Monetization`

**Measure:** Payer conversion; ARPDAU; ARPPU

**Pitfalls:** Optimising revenue while D7 retention falls

### P1 · Fairness & player trust

> “to be greedy instead of wanting to make a fun experience and from what I've heard the Roblox algorithm seems to push games that make a lot of money which in turn makes the game more popular and thus makes more money regardless of if …”  
> — [BinzuDev – How I Learned To Make Roblox Games in a Week @ 37:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vUN2cJD4mUk&t=2229s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Sell time savings, convenience and cosmetics; keep competitive outcomes skill-based.
1. Make every paid advantage reachable through play, slower.

**Measure:** Retention of non-payers; Review / like ratio

**Pitfalls:** Pay-to-win perception driving away the non-paying majority

> “Most beginners, like myself, assume you need to be some sort of insane 3D artist before you can make your first game, but you really don't.”  
> — [DitchyDevelopments – How To Make Your First Roblox Game in 2026 (With AI) @ 1:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v8vby3iOOX4&t=95s) · YouTube

> “to be greedy instead of wanting to make a fun experience and from what I've heard the Roblox algorithm seems to push games that make a lot of money which in turn makes the game more popular and thus makes more money regardless of if …”  
> — [BinzuDev – How I Learned To Make Roblox Games in a Week @ 37:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vUN2cJD4mUk&t=2229s) · YouTube

> “make sure to check them out I have a bunch of videos explaining my development journey and essentially I'm a front page developer I earned about like 200 Grand in commissions uh totally across these two years and I'm like”  
> — [VuukStudios – How To Make A Combat System In Roblox Studio [BEGINNER TUTORIAL] @ 27:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ht6ZfibXpDs&t=1648s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Optimise the signals the recommender reads: play-through, play days and playtime per user (D1, D2-D7, D8-D28), co-play days, spend days and Robux spend.
1. Fix first-play bounce before buying traffic; recommendations expand to cohorts that engage.
1. Strength in both retention and monetisation earns broader distribution than either alone.

**APIs / tools:** `Creator Hub Analytics: Acquisition`

**Measure:** Home impressions; Play-through rate; D1/D7 retention

**Pitfalls:** Chasing impressions with a game that does not retain

### P1 · Paid acquisition

> “So instead of just going out and you know putting a YouTube sponsor like before this video for example, they can build something that's interactive in Roblox and that's the new way to make people into kind of lifelong fans.”  
> — [Starter Story – I Spent 24 Hours With Roblox Millionaires @ 4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xgnm6SynH4&t=295s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Buy ads/sponsorships to test the funnel at scale once D1 retention is healthy.

**APIs / tools:** `Ads Manager (Creator Hub)`

**Measure:** Cost per play; Paid-cohort D7 retention

**Pitfalls:** Scaling spend before onboarding works

### P1 · External content & creators

> “Uh, no. If we want our game to go viral, we need to make sure it feels good to play.”  
> — [Duckable – Can I Make a VIRAL TYCOON in 24 HOURS? @ 14:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F9sfnpkzcPw&t=871s) · YouTube

**Build on Roblox** *(curated playbook)*:

1. Seed short-form clips of the most shareable moment; give creators reasons to record (events, codes, secrets).

**Measure:** Traffic by source (Acquisition dashboard)

**Pitfalls:** Spikes from content that the game cannot retain

## Method

1. **Discover** — YouTube search per pillar query (yt-dlp), TikTok creator feeds, curated first-party doc pages, DevForum (Discourse API).
2. **Rank** — video score = performance × (0.25 + 0.75 × relevance), where performance = 0.55 view-velocity + 0.25 like-rate + 0.20 channel authority (min-max normalised) and relevance is taxonomy fit scaled by a developer-intent signal, so viral gameplay videos cannot outrank design content. Docs have a fixed first-party score.
3. **Fetch** — caption tracks via yt-dlp (manual > original-language ASR; machine translations rejected); docs article text.
4. **Extract** — sentence segmentation (punctuation, pauses, discourse markers) → taxonomy classification → actionability scoring (directives, imperatives, causal reasoning, numbers) → merged evidence passages.
5. **Synthesise** — per mechanic: distinct-source support, weighted by source performance and actionability; P0/P1/P2 tiers; curated Roblox playbook attached; stale advice checked against first-party deprecation notices.

**Limitations.** Popularity is not correctness: high-performing videos can still be wrong, which is why first-party docs are weighted in and stale-advice checks run. The heuristic extractor favours explicit advice; implicit lessons (shown, not said) need the Claude extractor (`bpe analyze --extractor claude`).
